Wait, the last 8 bytes are `a\na\n\n   ` which means the last line is `   ` (3 spaces) preceded by a newline. But the line before the last line is `a\n`, so the structure is:

```
...
a
a
   
```

The last line is `   ` (3 spaces) at position 61-63. In `parse_fencedcode`, the loop processes lines:

- `line_start = 61` (start of the last line)
- `while (i < size && data[i] != '\n') i++;` → `i = 64` (no newline found, `i >= size`)
- `w2 = is_codefence(data + 61, 3, ...)` → `data[3] = text->data[64]` which is past the buffer!

Wait, but the loop at line 2291 is:
```c
while ((line_start = i) < size) {
    while (i < size && data[i] != '\n')
        i++;
    w2 = is_codefence(data + line_start, i - line_start, ...);
    ...
    if (i < size) i++;
}
```

For the last line:
- `line_start = 61`, `i = 61` (from previous iteration)
- `while (i < size && data[i] != '\n') i++;` → `i = 64` (no newline, `i >= size`)
- `w2 = is_codefence(data + 61, 64 - 61 = 3, ...)` → `data[3] = text->data[64]` which is past the buffer!
